en.headline: Man dies after collapsing on Tsuen Wan Line train at Cheung Sha Wan
en.dek: A man in his 60s was found unresponsive on a morning train; service on the line was briefly delayed and platforms became crowded before normal operations resumed.
body: A man in his 60s collapsed on a Tsuen Wan Line train and was later certified dead at hospital, the MTR Corporation and police said on Thursday morning.

Police received a report from MTR staff at about 7.39am that a passenger had become unresponsive inside a train compartment at Cheung Sha Wan station. Ambulance officers took the man to Caritas Medical Centre, where he was certified dead at 8.47am.

The operator said train journeys between Central and Tsuen Wan required an extra 10 to 15 minutes while the incident was handled. Platforms at several stations filled with waiting passengers, and Tsuen Wan station was temporarily closed because of overcrowding. By about 8am the MTR said the matter had been dealt with and services were gradually returning to normal.
Police are investigating the cause of the man’s collapse. No further details on his identity or medical history were released.

zh.headline: 港鐵長沙灣站列車男乘客昏迷送院不治
zh.dek: 一名六旬男子今早在荃灣綫車廂內暈倒，送院後不治；荃灣綫服務一度受阻，多個車站月台擠迫，荃灣站曾關閉。
body: 港鐵及警方表示，今早一名六十多歲男子在荃灣綫列車上暈倒，其後送院不治。
警方於上午約7時39分接獲港鐵職員報案，指長沙灣站一列列車車廂內有男乘客昏迷。救護員到場後將男子送往明愛醫院，於上午8時47分證實不治。
港鐵表示，因應事件，來往中環與荃灣的行車時間預計需額外10至15分鐘。荃灣綫多個車站月台擠滿候車乘客，荃灣站因月台人數過多一度關閉。港鐵於上午約8時指事件已妥善處理，服務逐步回復正常。
警方正調查男子暈倒原因，未有公布其身份或病歷詳情。
